summary.headline: Rashi Peripherals Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 42% YoY to INR5,708 crores and PAT 172% to INR153 crores, with ~30% of H1 growth from price increases.
summary.overview: Management reported record Q2 and H1 FY27 profits on both standalone and consolidated bases, with consolidated Q2 revenue up 49% YoY to INR6,185 crores and PAT up 121% to INR131 crores. Growth was driven mainly by price increases and volume, with VDA Infosolutions (67% stake) consolidated for only about one month and the Restar JV semiconductor business also contributing one month. Operating cash flow was negative for the half and net debt to equity rose to 0.76x, which management attributed to inventory built ahead of the delayed Diwali season and VDA funding. A possible QIP of about INR900 crores was flagged as advance preparation for growth capital, drawing investor pushback on dilution of about 15%.

segments.name: Core ICT distribution
segments.commentary: About 10-11% of H1 growth from volume, ~30% from price increases, and ~10% from new businesses. Non-PC products (accessories, peripherals, CPUs, motherboards, hard drives) are more than 35-37% of business, which management says carries extra margin.

segments.name: VDA Infosolutions (enterprise IT, 67% stake)
segments.commentary: Consolidated from Q2 for about one month; under 2% of Q2 revenue and about 6 bps of EBITDA contribution. Management targets new businesses (VDA plus semiconductor) above 10% of top line, with bottom line more than 2x.

segments.name: Semiconductor and embedded (Restar JV)
segments.commentary: JV formalised, consolidated for one month in Q2. Rashi did about $20 million of semiconductor business last year; H1 FY27 is about 2x that, with FY27 guided to 3-4x last year. Management says segment margins are about 2x company level.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 price increases expected to contribute 10-15% growth (down from ~30% in H1), with DRAM prices expected to rise for at least another year and flash/HDD prices flattening.
H2 unit volume guided as roughly flattish: consumer units expected to decline, commercial flat to positive.
Management is confident of maintaining a good run rate in H2, citing VDA, Restar JV and new product lines and territories.
Sustainable EBITDA margin for FY29-FY30 taken as around 2.75% as a safe planning assumption.
Interest cost expected to stay in the same range as H1, including acquisition debt interest.
Enterprise business targeted at about 20% of business in FY27 and FY28; the company has largely stayed out of large AI data centre projects so far.
Debt-to-equity to be kept at up to 1:1 barring temporary ROCE-led exceptions; a fresh raise of ~INR900 crores (QIP) is under preparation and may not happen.
capex_capacity: QIP preparation of about INR900 crores flagged as growth capital for capacity; management said at 1:1 debt-equity it would add INR1,800-2,000 crores of deployable capital and support INR12,000-15,000 crores of additional revenue on a 6-7x working capital cycle.
Inventory built in Sept-Oct to secure supply and committed enterprise and AI projects; management plans to convert it to cash in H2 and report progress next quarter.
Depreciation run rate after VDA consolidation is about INR12 crores per quarter, including intangibles amortisation; ESOP cost in Q2 was INR3.8 crores.
Restar JV plans a design centre in Bangalore with one Restar engineer deputed to train the team; Restar has around 200 engineers in Tokyo.
demand_pricing: IDC reported India PC market grew about 12% in April-June quarter, led by commercial, education and small business demand, with premium and AI-capable notebooks.
Management flagged that part of channel buying was ahead of price increases and that higher prices are hitting consumer affordability; commercial is about 70% of India's ICT market.
Deepavali shifted from 20 October (2025) to 8 November (2026), delaying the cycle about one month; October sales were described as very good and the current week continues strong.
Semiconductor distribution opportunity in India estimated at about INR25,000 crores; Restar's market reach estimated at about 10% of opportunity, leaving about 90% unserved.
Post-COVID price correction of 10-15% did not hurt distribution; Rashi grew about 7% while the market declined about 15%, per the CEO.
Enterprise and AI data centre orders of more than INR20,000 crores were placed in the last quarter; Rashi chose not to bid aggressively.
Management said it had 89 global brands, 10,280 channel partners, 57 branches, 50 service centres and 728 locations.

qa_highlights.question: Why was inventory built so strongly this quarter given softening consumer demand, and why a QIP of about INR900 crores (~15% dilution)?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory was built for the Diwali timing shift (one-month delay) and October sales were strong; management called the consumer impact minuscule. The QIP is advance preparation for growth capital and may not be done if not needed; an analyst suggested a calibrated raise instead.

qa_highlights.question: Split of growth between volume, price and VDA?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 growth of about 50% was split roughly 30% price, 10-11% volume and about 10% new businesses. VDA contributed under 2% of Q2 revenue.

qa_highlights.question: How is margin resilient in a seasonally strong quarter, and how much is value-led?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited strong demand, price increases reducing market price competition, and a non-PC mix (35-37%) with margin opportunities. It said the margin is sustainable near term.

qa_highlights.question: What does the Restar JV bring and is it exclusive?
qa_highlights.answer: It brings Japanese brands (two large ones already added, distribution starting this month), design capability, and access to Japanese manufacturers in India (meetings with 5 this month). Arrangements may be a mix of exclusive and non-exclusive; names not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Price outlook for H2 and risk of price correction?
qa_highlights.answer: Price contribution to growth is expected at 10-15% in H2 versus ~30% in H1. DRAM prices are expected to rise for at least another year, while flash and HDD have flattened.

qa_highlights.question: Debt-to-equity and funding plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Target is up to 1:1 debt-equity; the current 0.76x net debt-to-equity includes acquisition debt. Growth to be funded by internal accruals, debtor factoring and, if required, a capital raise. September quarter is the peak for borrowings.

risks_watch: Negative operating cash flow for H1 and net debt to equity of 0.76x; management promised inventory conversion progress next quarter.
Consumer demand expected to decline in units in H2; price increases are expected to slow to 10-15% contribution.
Possible QIP of about INR900 crores (~15% dilution) and investor reaction to its size and timing.
Integration of VDA (67% stake) and the newly formed Restar semiconductor JV; execution and retention of staff and clients.
Large enterprise and AI data centre projects were not pursued aggressively, so H2 contribution from this area is uncertain.
Sharp increase in intangibles from the VDA acquisition, with goodwill below 20% of the total intangibles.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and margins, but explicitly cautious on consumer demand and credit; management acknowledged cash flow and leverage pressure and framed it as deliberate. Several answers on the QIP size, JV exclusivity and AI exposure were general or deferred until formalisation.
key_quotes: So, the expansion is coming from mix and pricing discipline, not only operating leverage.
Converting the cash inventory into cash in the second half is a priority, and we will report on our progress next quarter.
So, the impact so far is miniscule.
Broadly, it is 2x on margin front.

adds.what: Restar JV design centre in Bangalore (engineering capacity, not production capacity)

growth.why: H2 FY27 growth guided via price increases of 10-15% and flattish units, with semiconductor/VDA targeted above 10% of top line and semiconductor FY27 at 3-4x last year; backing is partial as no hard capacity or order numbers were given beyond a QIP of ~INR900 crore under preparation that may not happen.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 standalone EBITDA margin rose 95 bps YoY to 3.44% and H1 to 3.28%, but management plans around 2.75% sustainable for FY29-FY30, implying H2 margins are not guaranteed to hold at the Q2 level.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: A ~INR900 crore QIP is under preparation for growth capital, which at 1:1 debt-equity would add INR1,800-2,000 crore of deployable capital supporting INR12,000-15,000 crore of revenue, but the raise may not happen; the Bangalore Restar design centre is engineering, not production, capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H2 unit volume is guided roughly flattish, with consumer units expected to decline and only commercial flat to positive, versus about 10-11% volume growth in H1.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management is preparing a ~INR900 crore QIP for growth capital, but utilisation was not disclosed and the company is asset-light distribution, so the call hinges on the QIP going ahead.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: H2 price contribution is guided down to 10-15% from ~30% in H1 and units flattish, so growth guidance is more likely to moderate than rise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 operating cash flow was negative, net debt to equity rose to 0.76x, consumer units are expected to fall in H2, and price-led growth roughly halves to 10-15%, though management is confident of maintaining a good H2 run rate.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management cites new product lines and territories, including two large Japanese brands added via the Restar JV with distribution starting this month, and semiconductor FY27 targeted at 3-4x last year's roughly $20 million base.

rows.label: Inventory conversion to cash in H2
rows.why: Working capital days fell to 55 from 61 a year ago, and management plans to convert the Sept-Oct inventory build to cash in H2 and report progress next quarter, but H1 operating cash flow was negative.

rows.label: Semiconductor and VDA above 10% of top line
rows.why: Management targets new businesses above 10% of revenue with bottom line more than 2x, and semiconductor H1 is about 2x last year's ~$20 million, guided to 3-4x for FY27.

rows.label: Enterprise and AI data centre participation
rows.why: Enterprise and AI orders above INR20,000 crore were placed last quarter but Rashi chose not to bid aggressively, though it still targets enterprise at about 20% of business.

tone.note: Management was confident on record profits, margins and the Restar/VDA growth push, but cautious on consumer demand, cash flow and leverage; analysts pressed on the ~INR900 crore QIP dilution (~15%), inventory build, and JV exclusivity and AI exposure, which were answered only generally.
